1001994.etyen:
The precise origin of the female given name is uncertain. Several origins have been proposed. First attested in the c. 1880.
One possibility is a Nordic adaptation of Irish Irish Eithne, from Middle Irish Eithne, from Old Irish Eithne. The Middle Irish name is traditionally associated with eitne (“grain, kernel”).
A second possibility is formation as a female counterpart of Enar, belonging to the same name family as Einar. Old Norse Einarr is probably formed from *ainaz (“one, single”), from *h₁óynos (“one, single”), and *harjaz (“warrior”), from *kóryos (“war, troops”), ultimately from *ker-

1005066.etyen:
From Bottolf (“male given name”) + -sen (“patronymic suffix meaning “son of””), originally a patronymic meaning “son of Bottolf”.
The given name Bottolf is a variant of Botolv, ultimately from Old Norse Bótólfr, a name formed from bót (“remedy, help, improvement”) and úlfr (“wolf”), literally “remedy-wolf”.
The surname spelling Bottolfsen is attested in Norwegian records by the 19th century. It originally functioned as a true patronymic but later became established as a hereditary family name.
